title: Unequal Uncertainty: Rethinking Algorithmic Interventions for Mitigating Discrimination from AI

bias_targets.methodology: Socio-technical and legal analysis evaluating how uncertainty thresholds in AI-assisted consumer credit decisions can act as proxies for gender (e.g., female loan applicants), leading to direct and indirect discrimination under UK law.

Theoretical evaluation using case studies in consumer credit and content moderation to show how selective algorithmic interventions (abstention and friction) disproportionately penalize communities of color due to higher predictive uncertainty.

Analyzing the disparate impact of algorithmic interventions in AI-assisted content moderation, specifically examining how models assigning lower confidence to queer content leads to disproportionate shadowbanning and unlawful discrimination.
Evaluating the socio-technical consequences of content moderation algorithms that struggle with nuances and disproportionately flag non-English posts due to under-representation in training data.
